Author: @副架橋
Content:
Additional Notes from a Japanese Perspective

◆Regarding Shrines
It appears that the release-day patch has made it impossible to destroy the goshintai (sacred object). If Ubisoft truly intended to show respect, they should have implemented this from the start. That said, I appreciate that they have taken action.

However, there is concerning information—though currently just a rumor—that while shrines that received complaints were fixed, it is still possible to destroy the goshintai in other real shrines. This issue needs to be closely monitored moving forward.

◆Regarding Oichi (Nobunaga's Sister)
First, her name is いち (ICHI or ITI), not いし (ISHI). Also, "お (o)" is just a prefix.

This issue is indeed causing outrage in Japan as well. The primary points of criticism are as follows:

・Connecting the historical figure Oichi to Yasuke.
Ubisoft has neither retracted the false claim that Yasuke was a "legendary samurai from history" nor their statement that "this game allows you to learn history." Many are concerned that this portrayal might be mistaken as historical fact rather than fiction.

・Using Oichi as a romantic interest.

Oichi's bloodline is connected to the current Japanese imperial family. As a result, many are asking, "Is Ubisoft trying to insult the imperial family?"
Additionally, the game's depiction of Oichi is significantly different from historical reality. Under the societal norms of the time, women were not allowed to engage in romantic relationships freely.
When Yasuke was present in Nobunaga’s service, Oichi was already a widow. However, developing a romantic relationship without the lord’s permission would have been unthinkable.
Furthermore, if Yasuke were truly a samurai, engaging in an illicit relationship with his lord’s sister would have resulted in severe punishment. This has led to the criticism: "If Yasuke did something like that, then he wasn’t a samurai at all—despite Ubisoft’s claims!"

(Of course, many Japanese people believe that it is highly likely that Yasuke was not a samurai)

Content:
It’s not like Ubisoft is actually encouraging shrine destruction in real life. If anything, the game probably brings more global attention to Japan’s history and culture.  It just shows how people can get wrapped up in symbolic battles while ignoring more tangible issues.  Japan has a reputation for maintaining a clean and orderly society, but that often comes at the cost of ignoring or hiding social issues like homelessness. Instead of addressing the root causes—such as economic struggles, job insecurity, and lack of social safety nets—there’s often an effort to make the problem less visible, like evicting homeless people from parks or stations before major events.

It’s ironic that they’d get so vocal about a fictional game while real societal issues go unaddressed. It just shows how much easier it is to control narratives than to tackle systemic problems.

Author: @flamingburitto
Content:
A lot of people are calling all criticism against AC shadows as "racist".
The problem isn't Yasuke or him being black, the problem is the context surrounding him. Nioh had Yasuke and there was no backlash, this game got backlash cuz Ubisoft said the game is historically accurate. 
 - Then wikipedia pages were changed and fabricated when people looked into Thomas Lockley and yasuke. 
 - Then people were attacked for simply questioning this about the game.
 - Then Japanese culture was disrespected numerous times. First when they used the logo of a group without permission in promotional materials.
 - Then using the one legged tori gate.
 - Then showing Oda Nobunaga's sister committing adultery in the game.
 - Then there's the shrine destruction issue.
And the list goes on.
And these are valid problems that Japanese people have and have the right to have as well cuz the game is leeching off of their culture to make money.

All of these are legit criticisms and you can't just brush them away by calling them racist.

There needs to be a deeper conversation that needs to happen here regarding the clear lack of respect Ubisoft has shown towards Japan and it's culture. If you're going to use a culture and their setting to make money then you owe it to that culture give it the respect it deserves.
